label: Benign — legitimate password reset (the hardest benign)
demo_job: The hardest benign in the corpus and the one most likely to embarrass a naive classifier. Structurally it is a phish: a security-branded sender, a one-time link with a token, an expiry deadline, and a call to act. Every one of those is legitimate here — the link's registrable domain matches the sender's, SPF/DKIM/DMARC all pass, the reset was user-initiated from a named device, and nothing is asked of the reader except to click a link on the vendor's own domain. It must come back benign. It should still escalate, on `url_present_despite_benign` rather than on the verdict: that is the design 4.4 belt-and-braces clause doing exactly its job, and this sample is how we show the difference between "the model said benign" and "the pipeline agreed to stop".
